title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: Both Gulf sea exits are now contested: the Houthis hold the Bab el-Mandeb after Yemeni government forces pulled back on Sunday, and another tanker was attacked near Hormuz. In the air, Gulf capacity is still 18% below pre-war and Middle East spot rates are up 61-73% on the year, while Qatar Airways is back in Riyadh before the UAE carriers.

stories.headline: Houthis take control of the Bab el-Mandeb as Yemeni forces withdraw
body: Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces are pulling back from Dhubab Airport and the Bab el-Mandeb area toward Aden, Reuters reported on Sunday. That leaves the Iran-backed Houthis in control of the strait at the southern end of the Red Sea.

The Houthis have already struck Saudi ports, airports and Aramco sites, including Yanbu. With Iran still disrupting Hormuz, Reuters says this would further isolate Gulf producers from their main shipping routes.
stories.soWhat: New: the Red Sea exit is now in hostile hands too. Routings via Jeddah and Saudi west-coast ports, used as a Hormuz bypass, carry more risk.

stories.headline: Tanker attacked near Hormuz; Bahrain shoots down Iranian drones
body: UKMTO said a tanker was attacked on Sunday while sailing east in the Gulf just before entering Hormuz. The crew are safe. Bahrain's air defences intercepted Iranian drones early on Sunday, its first interceptions since September; the IRGC said it fired six drones at a US radar site.

CENTCOM said on Saturday that more than 1.7 billion barrels of crude have moved through Hormuz under US protection. The US naval blockade on Iran stays in place. Iran's foreign minister is due in Muscat on Tuesday for talks with Oman.
stories.soWhat: Attacks went on over the weekend. Tuesday's Muscat talks are the next thing that could move war-risk costs, up or down.

stories.headline: Gulf air capacity still 18% down; Middle East rates up 61-73%
body: WorldACD says Arabian Gulf capacity is still 18% below pre-war levels, with flights to and from Riyadh near shutdown. The worldwide average spot rate was $3.67/kg in October, up 37% on the year, and Middle East & South Asia rates rose 61% in the latest two weeks.
In week 46, Europe-origin spot rates jumped 10% on the week to $2.71/kg. Middle East & South Asia spot rates were 73% above last year.
stories.soWhat: Air capacity in and out of the Gulf is still scarce and expensive. This is not the time to discount air rates.

stories.headline: Qatar Airways back in Riyadh; UAE carriers still out
body: Qatar Airways resumed daily Riyadh flights on 13 November and planned Dammam for 14 November, India News Network reported. Etihad passenger and cargo flights to Riyadh and Dammam stay cancelled until at least 19 November.
Emirates has not confirmed a restart. Its booking system showed Riyadh and Dammam flights scheduled from 28 November, Deep Arrival reported.
stories.soWhat: New: a Gulf rival is flying Riyadh again while UAE belly capacity is not. UAE-Riyadh road stays our main option for at least two more weeks.

stories.headline: Gulftainer buys 1,000 trucks and plans auto logistics park in KAFEZ
body: Gulftainer signed with United Al Saqer Heavy Equipment for 1,000 trucks. The first 450 arrive before end-November and the rest in Q1 2027. United Al Saqer will run the largest truck workshop on the UAE east coast, at Al Dhaid in KAFEZ.
The two also agreed to build a 100,000 sq m automotive logistics park in KAFEZ.
stories.soWhat: A second port operator is building its own truck fleet for the east-coast routes. Expect more land-bridge capacity and pressure on trucking rates.

competitors.name: Emirates SkyCargo
competitors.headline: Adds Milan-New York freighter after 52% revenue jump
body: From 5 December SkyCargo will fly a weekly Boeing 777 freighter from Milan to New York JFK, about 100 tonnes a flight, plus a weekly Milan-Dubai freighter. Its freighter network grew from over 40 destinations in March to over 60 in July.
In April-September, cargo revenue rose 52% while tonnage fell 1% to 1.24 million tonnes. The chairman said jet fuel prices doubled on the year.
competitors.soWhat: SkyCargo is earning on yield, not volume, and flying freighters outside the Gulf. Our air buy rates from Dubai will stay high; protect our own margins.

competitors.name: Gulftainer
competitors.headline: Moves into trucking with a 1,000-vehicle fleet
body: Gulftainer, which runs Khor Fakkan and Sharjah ports, is buying 1,000 trucks, 450 of them by end-November. It follows DP World, which runs more than 3,000 trucks on the east-coast bypass.
competitors.soWhat: Both big port groups now sell land transport with their berths. We compete on door-to-door service and customs, not on the truck leg alone.

competitors.name: Aramex (baseline)
competitors.headline: Launches Data Center Logistics across GCC, Asia and US
body: Aramex Data Center Logistics handles construction kit, AI racks and on-site delivery for data centres. It starts in the GCC, Southeast Asia, Taiwan and the US South, naming Abu Dhabi, Riyadh, Johor, Texas and Louisiana. A crated AI rack weighs about 1.75 tonnes. The GCC network has more than 7,000 people.
competitors.soWhat: We now have a product to answer SkyCargo's AI Tech launch. Sales needs a target list of Abu Dhabi and Riyadh data-centre projects.

opportunities.title: Riyadh by road, for longer
opportunities.text: Etihad is off Riyadh and Dammam to at least 19 November and Emirates shows a 28 November restart. Keep selling the UAE-Riyadh road service.

opportunities.title: Air yield on Gulf lanes
opportunities.text: Gulf capacity is 18% down and Middle East spot rates are up 61-73%. Sell space we hold at market rates.

opportunities.title: Data-centre projects
opportunities.text: Our Data Center Logistics product names Abu Dhabi and Riyadh. Pitch it to contractors before SkyCargo sells direct.

opportunities.title: More east-coast trucks to buy from
opportunities.text: Gulftainer adds 450 trucks this month. More capacity can lower our subcontract trucking cost on the land bridge.

watchouts.title: Red Sea exit in Houthi hands
watchouts.text: Bab el-Mandeb control raises risk on Red Sea and Saudi west-coast routings we use around Hormuz.

watchouts.title: Attacks continue
watchouts.text: A tanker was hit near Hormuz and Bahrain shot down drones on Sunday. Muscat talks on Tuesday could swing costs.

watchouts.title: Doha takes Saudi cargo
watchouts.text: Qatar Airways flies Riyadh again while UAE carriers do not. Saudi-bound air shippers may route via Doha.

watchouts.title: Port groups on the land leg
watchouts.text: DP World and Gulftainer both now run big truck fleets. Expect bundled port-plus-truck offers in freight tenders.

moves.title: Check Red Sea routings this week
moves.text: List live shipments routed via Jeddah or the Red Sea and brief key accounts on the Bab el-Mandeb risk.

moves.title: Keep the Riyadh road rate live to 28 November
moves.text: Etihad is out to 19 November and Emirates shows 28 November. Extend the offer and tell customers.

moves.title: Hold Gulf air surcharges
moves.text: Capacity is 18% down and rates are still rising. No air rate cuts on Gulf lanes this month.

moves.title: Re-tender east-coast trucking
moves.text: Ask Gulftainer's partner and other hauliers for rates as the first 450 trucks arrive.

moves.title: Build a data-centre target list
moves.text: Map Abu Dhabi and Riyadh data-centre builds and pitch Data Center Logistics to their contractors.

moves.title: Prepare two rate scenarios for Muscat
moves.text: Draft surcharge settings for talks failing or progressing, so we can move within a day.

note: Read from today's news. Check against our own numbers before acting.
